meta.title: ACARD score — 30-day mortality after status epilepticus
meta.authors: Lattanzi S, Trinka E, Bosque-Varela P, et al., Meletti S
meta.outcome: Risk of death within 30 days of the onset of non-hypoxic status epilepticus, from the Age–Consciousness–Aetiology–Refractoriness–Disability (ACARD) score.
meta.cff_info:
What this shows. The ACARD score (Age, Consciousness, Aetiology, Refractoriness, Disability) estimates the risk of death within 30 days of the onset of non-hypoxic status epilepticus (SE) in adults (Lattanzi et al., Neurology 2026).

How it is scored. Five routinely-available items are added: age ≥75 (+3), stupor/coma before treatment (+1), acute-primary-CNS aetiology (+2) or remote aetiology (−2), refractoriness to treatment (+3) and pre-existing disability (mRS ≥3, +2). The total ranges from −2 to +11; each total maps to a published 30-day-mortality estimate.

Validation. Derived in 689 SE episodes (Modena, Italy; 30-day mortality 27.3%) and externally validated in 569 episodes (Salzburg, Austria; 11.6%), with strong discrimination (AUC 0.864 derivation, 0.845 validation) and good calibration. It outperformed STESS, mSTESS, EMSE and SACE. The optimal cut-off is ≥6 points (sensitivity 69%, specificity 84%): 88% of patients scoring <6 survived, while 63% scoring ≥6 died.

Scope. Adults / adolescents (≥14 years) with non-hypoxic SE. A group-level tool — it should support, not replace, clinical judgement, and must not by itself justify limiting life-sustaining care. Population-level estimates.

predictors.name: Age ≥ 75 years
predictors.assess: Is the patient aged 75 years or older at SE onset? (Data-driven optimal cut-off in the derivation cohort.)

predictors.name: Consciousness before treatment
predictors.assess: Level of consciousness before SE treatment, using the STESS categorisation. Stupor or coma adds a point.

predictors.name: Aetiology of status epilepticus

options.label: Acute — primary CNS (cerebrovascular, active CNS infection, head trauma)
Other (acute-secondary CNS, acute-toxic, triggering factors, progressive, unknown)

predictors.assess: Underlying cause. Acute-primary-CNS pathology carries the highest risk (+2); a remote symptomatic cause is protective (−2); all other aetiologies score 0.

predictors.name: Refractoriness to treatment
predictors.assess: Refractory SE = persistence despite first-line benzodiazepine plus one second-line ASM. Available early in the episode, though not at the very onset.

predictors.name: Disability before SE (mRS ≥ 3)
predictors.assess: Pre-existing functional disability, modified Rankin Scale ≥3 before the SE episode.

model.note: 30-day mortality by ACARD total (Lattanzi 2026, Figure 2). A group-level prognostic tool — interpret alongside the full clinical picture; do not use it alone to justify withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment.
model.viz_info: Age, consciousness, aetiology, refractoriness and disability each add (or subtract) points; the waterfall shows the build-up from the lowest-risk profile. The total maps to the published 30-day mortality shown in the donut.
model.ci_note: * one-sided 97.5% CI (score with 0% or 100% observed mortality).

provenance.source: Lattanzi et al., Neurology 2026;107(3):e218281 (doi 10.1212/WNL.0000000000218281). Point values from Table 2; per-score 30-day-mortality estimates and 95% CIs from the Figure 2 companion table (exact printed values, not digitized).
provenance.notes: ACARD = Age(≥75 +3) / Consciousness(stupor-coma +1) / Aetiology(acute-primary-CNS +2, remote −2, other 0) / Refractoriness(+3) / Disability(mRS≥3 +2). Score −2..+11. pct = 30-day mortality per Fig 2 table. Baseline (all-minimum) profile is remote-aetiology, <75, alert, non-refractory, mRS<3 → 0%. Externally validated (AUC 0.845).
